title: Teeth wear and clarinet playing
summary: They compare dental wear from biting the mouthpiece, including George Lewis's false teeth.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, by the way, in regard to your teeth, did it ever wear your teeth at all through your lip? I guess it didn't. No. You never noticed any wear on your teeth then at all? Mm-mm. You still have your original teeth. I'm not trying to get personal or anything, but some people do play, George Lewis plays with false teeth in the helmet. Yeah. I think he said he's worn out one set of false teeth by just biting onto it. Yeah? I thought he'd bite them up, but I wasn't sure about it.
Yeah, he does. Yeah. Do you remember?
Oh. This way, it don't affect your teeth at all.
That vibration through your whole head, I guess, on the teeth too, would be good for you.

I noticed it when I first started, the first few times I blew it, I didn't know about the lip. I just popped my teeth on it. And I noticed the shape, but I thought it was all right. Yeah. And when I went to Mineta, well, of course, he'd tell me differently.
